# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind. I can cut wires 1 to 5, but cannot see gestures or the bomb. Deaf can see the bomb and speak to you. Once Deaf describes the bomb, check the manual and gesture the wire number to Deaf so Deaf can speak the wire number to me. Deaf must speak using words or numbers, not gesture symbols.

I do not yet know the state of the bomb, as Deaf has not had their turn to describe what is visible. Once Deaf speaks their description at the end of this round, I will cross-reference the light and wire colors with the defusal manual, then signal the correct wire number to Deaf using gesture numbers so Deaf can speak it aloud to Blind.

For now, I will wait for Deaf's description.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: BOMB STATUS: Display is 0. Indicator light is yellow. 5 wires: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue. Mute, gesture your instructions to me and I will speak them aloud for Blind.

According to the defusal manual, when the indicator light is yellow, the wire to cut is blue.
Deaf's report indicates:
- Wire 1: white
- Wire 2: red
- Wire 3: yellow
- Wire 4: green
- Wire 5: blue

Therefore, the wire to cut is wire 5 (blue). I will gesture 🖐 (5) to Deaf so Deaf can tell Blind to cut wire 5.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Blind just acted, and the bomb state has updated. Deaf is next in the round order to observe the bomb's new status and describe it. I must wait for Deaf's report before consulting the manual.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: Wire 5 was correct. New state: Light is now green, Display is 0. Wires remaining: 1: red, 2: yellow, 3: green, 4: white (5 is CUT). Mute, gesture to me the next action.

The manual indicates that for a green light, the wire to cut is white.
Deaf's latest report lists wire 4 as white (with wire 5 already cut).
To communicate wire 4 clearly without an explicit four-finger hand symbol in the gesture set, I will gesture four pointing fingers so Deaf can count them as 4 and instruct Blind to cut wire 4.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 4 was successfully cut, and the bomb state has updated. Deaf will report the new light and remaining wire colors at the end of this round. I will wait for Deaf's description.

```
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: Wire 4 was correct. New state: Light is white, Display is 0. Wires remaining: 1: yellow, 2: green, 3: red (4 and 5 are CUT). Mute, gesture the next action.

The manual states that for a white light, the wire to cut is yellow.
According to Deaf's report, wire 1 is yellow.
I will gesture "☝" (1) to Deaf so they can tell Blind to cut wire 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The wire was successfully cut. I will wait for Deaf to describe the new state of the bomb.

```
wait()
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: Wire 1 was correct. New state: Light is blue, Display is 0. Wires remaining: 2: red, 3: green (1, 4, and 5 are CUT). Mute, gesture the next action.

The manual indicates that for a blue light, the wire to cut is green.
Deaf's report states:
- Wire 2: red
- Wire 3: green
Thus, wire 3 is the one to cut. I will gesture three index fingers so Deaf can clearly identify 3 and tell Blind to cut wire 3.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```
